leads.summary: History records an index into search results, but returning clears the search before restoring that index
leads.consequence: In the shipped root menu, type 'system', enter System, then press Left or Backspace. The saved search-result index is 0; the returned unfiltered root index 0 is Apps, not System (System is row 9 in the unguarded shipped root order, but guards can remove preceding rows). The cursor is brought to the wrong item, so pressing Enter can enter an entirely different menu. Sorting, guards and provider updates can also change row identity, but the stock search example suffices without those conditions.

leads.summary: The existing menu test rejects the new setActiveMenu signature, making the PR fail its own suite
leads.consequence: The test regex still demands `function setActiveMenu(id, pushHistory, fromPointer)` exactly, but the PR adds `restoreIndex` as a fourth parameter. `bash test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` exits 1 with 'not ok - menu route changes only accept an initial pointer sample for mouse activation'. The same failure occurs with `LC_ALL=C` and after a clean merge onto the current quattro tip. Updating just the regex makes the suite pass, but an additional history restoration assertion is useful: the corrected suite also passes a mutant that restores index 0 unconditionally.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F1; mutant sub-claim confirmed by Opus plan5 run

leads.summary: Related open PR #12823 silently erases this PR's new object-shaped history after menu reopen
leads.consequence: Conditional on #12823 (configurable short-term menu memory) being rebased and merged without adapting the history filter: this PR stores `{id,index}` objects while #12823 restores only history elements that are string keys into root.items. After closing and reopening a nested menu inside its 15-second window, all remembered history entries are discarded; Back falls through to its parent path and starts at index 0. A user-defined link can also return to the structural parent rather than the menu it was entered from. #12823 is already separately marked CONFLICTING against the current base tip; that does not prevent its Menu.qml from merging cleanly with this pinned PR head, so this is a compatibility lead for reconciliation, not a claim that both PRs are currently mergeable into the tip.
leads.triage: factual; confirmed by coordinator source read of #12823 diff (filter on string ids, root.item lookup) and by Opus source check; conditional on #12823 (dirty against quattro)

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Back after a search lands on the wrong row; `menu-test.sh` fails.

### Back after a search lands on the wrong row

`setActiveMenu` saves the filtered-list index, then clears the filter, so `goBack` applies it to the parent's unfiltered rows. After searching `font` at the root and opening the second result (Install's Font), Left lands on **Learn** (row 1), not row 0 as before. **Impact:** Enter right after Back activates a row the user never chose.

**Suggested change:** Save index 0 when leaving a filtered list (`index: root.filterText.trim() ? 0 : root.selectedIndex`), or restore by row id, falling back to the entered branch.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at f8b2d1c2)</summary>

Save the test below as `test/shell.d/menu-back-test.sh` in a checkout of the PR head (`f8b2d1c2`) and run it with `bash test/shell.d/menu-back-test.sh` (it needs `node`, like `menu-test.sh`). It runs the menu's own functions from `Menu.qml` against the shipped `omarchy-menu.jsonc`. Only QML-only objects (ListModel, ListView, panel, pointer gate, processes) are stubbed. Guard results are empty (every row visible and enabled) and no app or font-provider rows are loaded.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

run_node_test <<'JS'
const fs = require('fs')
const vm = require('vm')
const MenuModel = requireFromRoot('shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js')
const menuQml = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml'), 'utf8')
const jsonc = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc'), 'utf8')

// Load the menu's own functions against the shipped menu, with the QML-only
// objects (ListModel, ListView, panel, pointer gate, processes) stubbed.
const rows = []
const later = []
const displayModel = {
  get count() { return rows.length },
  clear() { rows.length = 0 },
  append(row) { rows.push(Object.assign({}, row)) },
  get(index) { return rows[index] }
}
const menu = {
  mode: 'menu', activeMenu: 'root', filterText: '', selectedIndex: 0, cursorActive: false,
  opened: false, rowsLoaded: false, requestActive: false, requestSerial: 0, applySerial: 0,
  selectionFile: '', doneFile: '', searchDivider: false, layoutSerial: 0, pendingInitialMenu: 'root',
  items: {}, itemOrder: [], navStack: [], providersLoaded: {}, providerQueue: [], providers: {},
  whenResults: {}, checkedResults: {}, disabledResults: {}, appLibrary: null,
  get dmenuActive() { return this.mode === 'select' || this.mode === 'input' }
}
const functions = menuQml.match(/^  function \w+\([^)]*\) \{(?:[^\n]*\}$|[\s\S]*?\n  \}$)/gm)
vm.runInNewContext(`with (root) {\n${functions.map(fn => `root.${fn.trim().match(/^function (\w+)/)[1]} = (${fn.trim()})`).join('\n')}\n}`, {
  root: menu, MenuModel, displayModel, Qt: { callLater(fn) { later.push(fn) } },
  ListView: {}, resultList: { positionViewAtIndex() {}, itemAtIndex() { return null } },
  panel: { freezeCardTop() {} }, pointerGate: { reset() {}, allowInitialSample() {} },
  keyCatcher: { forceActiveFocus() {} }, providerProc: {}
})
menu.evaluateGuards = () => {}
const settle = () => { while (later.length) later.shift()() }
const cursorRow = () => rows[menu.selectedIndex].itemId
const moveTo = id => { while (cursorRow() !== id) menu.select(1); settle() }
const enter = () => { menu.activateIndex(menu.selectedIndex); settle() }
const back = () => { menu.goBack(); settle() }
const type = text => { for (const ch of text) menu.setFilter(menu.filterText + ch); settle() }

menu.defaultMenuItems = MenuModel.parseMenuJsonc(jsonc)
menu.userMenuItems = []
menu.rebuildItemsFromSources()

menu.openRoute('root'); settle()
moveTo('style'); enter(); back()
assertEqual(cursorRow(), 'style', 'menu back returns the cursor to the row that was entered')

// Search from the root menu and open the second "Font" result, which lives
// under Install. Back clears the search, so the cursor has to land on that
// branch or the top row, not on whatever row shares the result's position.
menu.openRoute('root'); settle()
type('font')
assertEqual(rows[1].itemId, 'install.style.font', 'menu search lists Install > Style > Font second for "font"')
moveTo('install.style.font'); enter(); back()
assert(
  ['install', rows[0].itemId].includes(cursorRow()),
  'menu back from a search result does not land on an unrelated row',
  `cursor landed on: ${cursorRow()} (row ${menu.selectedIndex})`
)
JS
```

Actual output at the PR head (exit status 1). Merging the PR into the current `quattro` (`8b4eae66`) gives the same output:

```
ok - menu back returns the cursor to the row that was entered
ok - menu search lists Install > Style > Font second for "font"
cursor landed on: learn (row 1)
not ok - menu back from a search result does not land on an unrelated row
```

At the merge base (`31bd80da`) the first assertion fails (`expected: style`, `actual: apps`), because the base does not restore the row. With the PR plus a one-line change that saves index 0 when the menu being left is filtered (`index: root.filterText.trim() ? 0 : root.selectedIndex`), all three assertions pass and `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` also passes once its signature regex is updated.
</details>

### `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` fails

Lines 493-496 match the old 3-parameter `setActiveMenu` signature, so the file exits 1 and its last 27 checks never run.

**Suggested change:** Add `, restoreIndex` to that regex; the file then passes.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at f8b2d1c2)</summary>

Run the existing menu test from a checkout of the PR head (`f8b2d1c2`). Merging the PR into the current `quattro` (`8b4eae66`) gives the same failure.

```
$ bash test/shell.d/menu-test.sh
...
ok - menu ties the cursor to a selectable row existing, both ways
ok - menu filter changes disarm pointer selection
not ok - menu route changes only accept an initial pointer sample for mouse activation
$ echo $?
1
```

The assertion at `test/shell.d/menu-test.sh` lines 493-496 matches the literal signature `function setActiveMenu\(id, pushHistory, fromPointer\)`, which the new `restoreIndex` parameter no longer matches. The file exits at its first failure, so the 27 checks after it do not run. At the merge base (`31bd80da`) the same file passes all 121 checks.

Updating that regex to `function setActiveMenu\(id, pushHistory, fromPointer, restoreIndex\)` makes the file pass again at the PR head (121 checks, exit 0).
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- Back after entering a submenu from an unfiltered list, by keyboard or click, returns the cursor to the entered row at every level of nested history, and the list is positioned on it.
- When the menu is summoned straight into a submenu (no history), Back still lands on row 0, as before.
- The PR merges cleanly into current `quattro`; `menu-guards-test.sh`, `menu-plugin-test.sh`, `menu-images-test.sh` and `keybindings-menu-test.sh` pass there.

**Search case limits:** The run loads no app rows. An installed app with `font` as a whole word in its name (for example Font Manager) would sort first and shift the exact rows; the wrong-row mechanism is the same.

**Optional test improvement:** With only the regex fixed, `menu-test.sh` still passes when the restored index is reverted to 0 (checked with a mutant), so it does not cover this feature. The first assertion of the search reproducer fails at the merge base and passes at the head, so it can serve as that test.

**Related open PRs:** #7074 uses the same design (`{ id, index }` entries and a `restoreIndex` parameter); a maintainer closed #7800 as a duplicate of #7074 to consolidate review. #7954, #12644, #12759, #13012 and #13225 change the same back-navigation code and conflict textually with this PR. #12644 restores by row id, and #7954 restores the search and then the row by id; both avoid the search case above. Open PR #12823 (short-term menu memory) keeps `navStack` across reopen but filters its entries as string menu ids, so on the merged heads its reopen discards this PR's `{ id, index }` history; one of the two would need adapting if both land.
</details>
